newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals mostly firm on yen's slip.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals mostly firm on yen's slip.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures settled mostly firmer on Wednesday, buoyed by the yen's slip against the dollar, traders said.
Only palladium futures ended weaker, reflecting a slump in spot palladium prices.
Gold futures ranged from one to five yen per gram firmer, with benchmark August finishing up two yen at 1,361 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from unchanged to seven yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was down one yen at 419 yen.
Private investors liquidated their longs in gold, while trade houses bought futures and sold spot gold in arbitrage.
Bullion was quoted at $381.00/30 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $381.00/381.50 in New York on Tuesday.
The spot gold market has so far reacted little to recent firmer crude oil prices, with gold moving within tight ranges during Asian hours, the traders said.
Traders were keeping eyes on U.S. consumer price data to be released later today, which may give direction to the market.
Gold bullion prices in the Tokyo spot market remained at a slight discount or nearly flat to world benchmark London, or loco London, reflecting weak physical gold demand in Japan.
For palladium, moderate bargain-hunting buying in the afternoon session prevented palladium futures from falling further, traders said.
But they said the Japanese market remained oversupplied with the metal. "It is a matter of time before spot palladium breaks through the next support at $115.0," one trader said.
Spot palladium was quoted at $116.00/75 per ounce at the Tokyo close. The benchmark August silver was up 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 183.1 yen. The benchmark August platinum was up one yen at 1,377 yen.
